opts: Liver enzymes, creatinine, platelets, LDH and a blood film for schistocytes
Thyroid function, a glucose tolerance test and an indirect Coombs test
A urine pregnancy test and nothing else beyond the blood pressure
Fetal karyotyping and a TORCH screen on maternal blood
exp: Ruling out HELLP needs haemolysis (LDH, film), liver involvement and a platelet count, with renal function included.

opts: Normal is 0.5-0.7; a value of 0.9 or more indicates transfusion need and higher mortality
Normal is 0.9-1.2; a value of 1.5 or more is the threshold for transfusion
Normal is 0.3-0.5; a value of 0.7 or more means she needs intensive care
Normal is 1.0-1.5; a value of 2.0 or more means hysterectomy is required
exp: The shock index is normally 0.5-0.7; 0.9 or above signals significant loss, the need for transfusion and raised mortality.

opts: A cup-like depression below the umbilicus, with a globular mass in the vagina and immediate shock
A hard contracted fundus, with the cervix easily visible and only slow bleeding
The fundus high above the umbilicus, with an empty vagina and fever
A Bandl's ring across the abdomen, with bulging membranes and late shock
exp: The fundus is absent abdominally or dimpled, a globular mass fills the vagina, and shock is immediate and out of proportion.

opts: As soon as the pregnancy is diagnosed by a positive urine pregnancy test
After delivery, once the placenta has been examined
Only from 36 completed weeks of gestation onwards
Before menarche, since the antibody persists for life
exp: Low-dose aspirin is started as soon as pregnancy is confirmed in women with antiphospholipid syndrome.

opts: A serum progesterone below 25 nmol/L on its own, without any imaging
Any positive pregnancy test, even when no ultrasound has been done
A ruptured ectopic, or an unruptured one that does not meet the prerequisites for medical treatment
Every stable unruptured ectopic, since surgery is always the safest option
exp: Surgery is indicated by rupture or instability, or when the criteria for methotrexate or expectant care are not met.

opts: Traction on the shoulders with malar flexion, the baby astride the operator's forearm
Traction in the groin with flexion of the neck from above
Fundal pressure from an assistant combined with jaw traction
Rotation of the trunk with suprapubic pressure applied to the head
exp: The Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit manoeuvre rests the baby on the forearm, flexes the head with fingers on the malar bones and applies shoulder traction.

opts: Lighter blades that grip well while compressing the fetal head less
Stronger traction through a wider surface of metal on the head
Rotation of the head by allowing the blades to slide independently
A better grip on the fetal scalp to prevent the blades slipping
exp: Fenestration lightens the blade and reduces the compressive force transmitted to the fetal head without losing grip.

opts: Kocher's forceps, with a single tooth, rat-like teeth, a ratchet lock and transverse serrations
Allis forceps, which are identified by several fine teeth on the jaws
A sponge holder, which is identified by its smooth, atraumatic jaws
An amnihook, which is identified by its single plastic hook
exp: Kocher's forceps has a single tooth at the tip with rat-like teeth, a ratchet lock and transverse serrations on the jaws.

q: Match the cervicograph zone to its meaning — green : yellow (alert) : pink (action).
opts: Normal progress : alert, so shift her to a tertiary centre : intervene once the action line is touched
Alert, so shift her : normal progress : intervene on touching the action line
Intervene at once : alert, so shift her : entirely normal progress
Normal progress : intervene at once : refer her to a tertiary centre
exp: Green means progress is normal, the alert zone means prepare for transfer, and touching the action line means intervention is required.

opts: Relief of breathing symptoms as the fetal head descends into the pelvis
The sudden onset of regular, painful uterine contractions
Rupture of the membranes before labour has begun
Effacement of the cervix during the last week of pregnancy
exp: Lightening is the relief of pressure symptoms when the presenting part descends, usually late in the third trimester.

opts: Formulae such as Hadlock or Shepherd, with abdominal circumference the most useful single parameter
Biparietal diameter and femur length measured in the second trimester
Head circumference combined with the placental grade
Three-dimensional volume measurement with the amniotic fluid index
exp: Composite formulae using abdominal circumference estimate fetal weight best, and abdominal circumference is the most sensitive parameter for growth restriction.

opts: The facial nerve, compressed against the maternal symphysis pubis
The ulnar nerve, compressed at the elbow during positioning
The phrenic nerve, stretched by the hyperflexed thighs
The lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh, compressed under the inguinal ligament
exp: Hyperflexing the thighs compresses the lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh under the inguinal ligament, causing meralgia paraesthetica.

opts: Stallworthy's sign, where the head cannot be pushed into the pelvis, with fetal distress
Cullen's sign, with bluish discolouration around the umbilicus
Chadwick's sign, with bluish discolouration of the vaginal mucosa
Bandl's sign, with a rising retraction ring across the abdomen
exp: In a posterior placenta previa the head is held up by the placental mass and cannot be pushed into the pelvis: Stallworthy's sign.

opts: Under general anaesthesia a hand is passed into the uterus, the feet are grasped and the fetus is turned to a breech
Under spinal anaesthesia the head is rotated with forceps before delivery
External manipulation through the abdomen with the membranes left intact
Traction on the cord under continuous ultrasound guidance in the labour ward
exp: Internal podalic version is an intrauterine manoeuvre under general anaesthesia, grasping a foot and converting the lie to a breech.

q: Match — restitution : external rotation of the head.
opts: Restitution: the neck untwists after delivery — external rotation: the shoulders turn one eighth of a circle
Restitution: the shoulders rotate one eighth — external rotation: the neck untwists
Restitution: the head extends as it is born — external rotation: the head flexes back
Restitution: descent through the cavity — external rotation: expulsion of the body
exp: Restitution untwists the neck after internal rotation, and external rotation then aligns the shoulders with the antero-posterior diameter.

opts: Early preterm labour only, with magnesium given only below 32 weeks; none in late preterm labour
Late preterm labour only, since early preterm delivery is inevitable
Both groups equally, with the same agents and the same neuroprotection
Only when chorioamnionitis has been confirmed on amniocentesis
exp: Tocolytics and magnesium belong to early preterm labour; neither has a place in late preterm labour.

opts: Terbutaline, salbutamol, ritodrine and isoxsuprine
Nifedipine and atosiban, which are calcium and oxytocin antagonists
Indomethacin and sulindac, which inhibit prostaglandin synthesis
Magnesium sulfate and progesterone, which are used for other purposes
exp: The beta-agonist group is terbutaline, salbutamol, ritodrine and isoxsuprine; the others belong to different drug classes.

opts: To measure the maternal blood glucose concentration during treatment
To confirm the diagnosis of pregnancy-induced hypertension
To judge whether the antibody level is high enough to cross the placenta and cause haemolysis
To determine the sex of the fetus before planning delivery
exp: A critical titre means there is enough antibody crossing the placenta to produce significant fetal haemolysis, and it triggers surveillance.

opts: All cases before 34 weeks, and from 34 weeks once chorioamnionitis and a previous course are excluded
Only below 28 weeks, since later gestation gains nothing
Only between 34 and 37 weeks, where the benefit is greatest
Every case regardless of infection, because the benefit outweighs the risk
exp: Corticosteroids are given before 34 weeks, and in the late preterm window once infection and prior treatment are excluded.

opts: Preterm labour before 34 weeks; no role after 34 weeks, in twins, or with chorioamnionitis
Preterm labour after 34 weeks only, with no role before 34 weeks
Twin pregnancy alone, with no role in singleton pregnancies
Chorioamnionitis alone, since infection shortens the cervix
exp: Tocolysis with steroids is for early preterm labour; it has no place in late preterm labour, twins or infection.

opts: Stop the oxytocin, turn her to the left, give oxygen, fluids if needed, then terbutaline
Increase the intravenous fluids and proceed to caesarean section
Continue the oxytocin with oxygen and prepare for forceps delivery
Give misoprostol and turn her into the left lateral position
exp: Tachysystole is managed by stopping the oxytocin, repositioning, oxygen and fluids, with a tocolytic such as terbutaline if it persists.

opts: WHO and ACOG advise delayed clamping; national guidance advises clamping once pulsation ceases; antiretrovirals matter more than timing
WHO advises early clamping and national guidance delayed clamping, with early clamping more protective
Both advise delayed clamping, and clamping timing matters more than antiretroviral therapy
Both advise early clamping, and early clamping reduces transmission more than antiretrovirals
exp: Delayed clamping is advised for HIV-positive mothers because transmission is driven by viral load, which antiretroviral therapy controls.

opts: Stable: ligation of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery — unstable: subtotal hysterectomy; then pelvic pressure packing
Stable: total hysterectomy — unstable: internal iliac ligation; then a gauze pack
Stable: embolisation — unstable: a B-Lynch suture; then a Bakri balloon
Stable: aortic ligation — unstable: oophorectomy; then a vaginal pack
exp: If she is stable, vessel ligation can preserve the uterus; if she is not, subtotal hysterectomy is faster and safer, with packing as a bridge.

opts: Vaginal mucosa, skin and subcutaneous tissue, the superficial perineal muscles and pudendal branches
The anal sphincter and the rectal mucosa, as in a fourth-degree tear
The levator ani muscle alone, with no skin or mucosal tissue
Bartholin's gland and the urethra, which lie within the incision line
exp: An episiotomy cuts vaginal mucosa, skin and subcutaneous tissue, the perineal muscles and branches of the pudendal vessels and nerve.

opts: Defective decidualisation, absence of Nitabuch's layer and excessive trophoblastic invasiveness
Hypertension, diabetes and cigarette smoking during pregnancy
Uterine overdistension, intrauterine infection and direct trauma
A thin myometrium, polyhydramnios and a twin pregnancy
exp: Accreta spectrum is a decidua problem plus an invasive trophoblast: no decidua, no Nitabuch layer, and over-invasive cytotrophoblast.

q: Recommendations for VBAC after a lower segment caesarean — ACOG : Indian national guidelines.
opts: ACOG: a trial may be offered whatever the number of scars — India: contraindicated with two or more previous sections
ACOG: permitted after one scar only — India: permitted after any number
ACOG: never offer a trial — India: offer it after two previous sections
ACOG: permitted after three scars — India: permitted after one scar only
exp: ACOG allows a trial after any number of low transverse scars after counselling; Indian guidance treats two or more as a contraindication.

opts: Creatinine falls to about 0.4-0.6 mg/dL, so a value above 0.8 mg/dL is abnormal in pregnancy
Creatinine rises to between 1.5 and 2.0 mg/dL from the increased filtration load
Creatinine stays fixed at about 1.0 mg/dL whatever the filtration rate
Creatinine becomes undetectable because filtration is so greatly increased
exp: With filtration up by half, creatinine falls; a value considered normal outside pregnancy is abnormal during it.

opts: An ultrasound Doppler transducer records the fetal heart rate and a tocodynamometer records contractions, with an event marker
A scalp electrode is attached directly to the fetal skull during the test
A pressure catheter is placed inside the amniotic cavity for the recording
Maternal pulse oximetry is recorded continuously alongside the fetal electrocardiogram
exp: External cardiotocography uses an abdominal Doppler transducer for the heart rate and a tocodynamometer for uterine activity.

opts: PPH: poor tone and heavy loss — inversion: a cup-like depression and a vaginal mass — AFE: both examination findings normal
PPH: entirely normal findings — inversion: poor uterine tone — AFE: a cup-like depression
PPH: a globular vaginal mass — inversion: heavy bleeding — AFE: poor uterine tone
All three conditions give entirely normal findings on both examinations
exp: Postpartum collapse is triaged by examination: bleeding with an atonic uterus, an inverted uterus felt in the vagina, or a normal examination with sudden collapse from embolism.

opts: A detailed fetal echocardiogram performed before 20 weeks
Amniocentesis, or external cephalic or internal podalic version
A DIPSI glucose tolerance test in the second trimester
A routine non-stress test in the third trimester
exp: Anti-D is given after any procedure that may cause feto-maternal haemorrhage, including amniocentesis and version.
